document.title: Infrared Forehead Thermometer Usability/Risk Evaluation Report

semantic_fragments.content: Normal USE SCENARIOS: OPERATOR/PATIENT = adult; room temperature; Adequate illumination; Measure the body temperature when the environment is quiet. Worst case USE SCENARIOS: PATIENT = OPERATOR; OPERATOR/PATIENT = adult; Environmental temperature is 40°C, 95%RH; inadequate illumination; Measure body temperature when the environment is unquiet.

The process of identifying known or foreseeable HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS in the context of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer project involves various steps and considerations. This activity is an integral part of the RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS, as outlined in ISO 14971, and is closely linked to the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS. HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS has been defined as when a USE SCENARIO of Infrared Forehead Thermometer leads to a potentially dangerous situation for operators. Preliminary HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS that encompass various stages of USER interaction with the Infrared Forehead Thermometer has been identified in section 4 of the risk assessment report, demonstrated as Hazardous situation. These scenarios include details about the sequence of events, conditions, environments, and descriptions of the user interface.

The purpose of selecting Hazard-Related Use Scenarios for summative evaluation in the context of a Infrared Forehead Thermometer is to ensure that the evaluation process covers all potential safety-related aspects of the device's user interface. The process involves determining which scenarios to include in the evaluation, considering factors like severity of harm, risks, and other circumstances specific to the device and the manufacturer. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate that users can safely and effectively interact with the Infrared Forehead Thermometer as intended. Given that a Infrared Forehead Thermometer is considered a simple device, and as a mature device, its use is not likely to result in severe harm, so all potential scenarios will be included in the summative evaluation, regardless of the severity of potential harm. This option would provide a comprehensive assessment of the device's user interface under various usage conditions and would likely cover a wide range of potential use errors.
